transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood DevRel), Aisha Khan (Sierra Head of ML), Tom Reyes (Cloud Infra), Natalie Vu (Security), Jorge Morales (Backend)

Summary:
Quick onboarding / walkthrough for Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript), authentication patterns (api keys vs KMS-wrapped keys), and VPC/private deployment considerations. Customer is planning pilot with PHI redaction in pipeline — security/compliance concerns drive decision. Goal: get sandbox integrated, validate KMS + VPC peering, run short latency/throughput POC.

Topics covered:
- SDK quickstart (py/ts) and env var secret handling
- KMS integration and key rotation patterns
- VPC peering and private deployment options
- Console walkthrough for billing/Optimize suggestions
- Benchmark plan and sample prompts for health domain

Action items (recap): see metadata list above for owners and due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everybody, thanks for taking the time today. we'll do a quick SDK walkthrough, show auth patterns and then go into VPC/KMS questions — how does that sound?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: yeah that sounds great, thanks. we've got a tight timeline so wanted to ensure we can get a sandbox up and running this week if possible.
[00:14] Tom Reyes: and to flag, our infra team needs exact CIDR ranges and peering steps before we open anything.
[00:19] Liam O'Rourke: absolutely, we'll include a terraform example. quick note, we'll show both simple api-key flow and the KMS-wrapped approach you asked about.
[00:27] Natalie Vu: just to clarify, when you say KMS-wrapped, do you mean Redwood-managed envelope keys or customer-managed keys in our KMS?
[00:34] Ravi Patel: good question — we support both. for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS (BYOK) and we show rotation patterns. for Hosted we offer an option to integrate your KMS via key wrapping so the master key never leaves your control.
[00:45] Jorge Morales: sorry quick interruption — will the SDK require us to change our CI secrets or can we use workload identity on GCP?
[00:52] Liam O'Rourke: you can use workload identity, yes. for GCP we recommend Workload Identity + short-lived tokens. for AWS we'll show IAM role chaining. we'll drop the samples.
[01:03] Aisha Khan: cool, can you show the python quickstart? that's what our ML team prefers.
[01:08] Maya Chen: sure — Ravi, you wanna share the code snippet?
[01:11] Ravi Patel: yeah I'll paste this up — (gulp) so python quickstart, pip install redwood-client, then set REDWOOD_API_KEY or export REDWOOD_KMS_KEY and use the client like: client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")) — note, in KMS flow you swap api_key with token_from_kms().
[01:28] [small laugh] Tom Reyes: token_from_kms, is that an SDK helper?
[01:31] Ravi Patel: yah it's an example helper we include in the repo. it handles the unwrap call to your KMS and then requests a short lived token from Redwood.
[01:39] Natalie Vu: does that mean the KMS credentials are only used in your helper and not sent to Redwood?
[01:43] Liam O'Rourke: correct — the helper contacts your KMS, unwraps locally, then exchanges for a short-lived Redwood token. we never persist your KMS key material. transcription note: sometimes the helper is 'KMS agent' in docs, which might read weird.
[01:55] Aisha Khan: hearing that is good. the other big point is VPC peering — we need to avoid egress to public internet for PHI. what's the recommended setup?
[02:03] Maya Chen: for Private deployments we provide a VPC connector. two patterns: 1) VPC peering with redwood-managed endpoints in customer region, or 2) customer-hosted gateway (on-prem). peering is simpler if your cloud allows it. we'll share exact CIDR and routing examples.
[02:16] Tom Reyes: our org restricts cross-account peering except via Transit Gateway. will that be a blocker?
[02:21] Liam O'Rourke: not a blocker — we can do Transit Gateway attachment or PrivateLink equivalents. depends on cloud, we'll map the pattern.
[02:29] Jorge Morales: any difference in performance between peering and PrivateLink?
[02:33] Liam O'Rourke: minimal for typical LLM inference, latency delta usually a few ms. throughput wise both fine — latency mostly depends on region and model size.
[02:41] [00:03:00] Maya Chen: switching gears to SDK environment setup — in TS you do npm i @redwood/inference and set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY. for KMS flow we provide a small cli that fetches wrapped token. here's an example snippet...
[03:15] Ravi Patel: (reads code) const client = new RedwoodClient({ token: process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN }); await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-13b-quant', messages: [...] }); 
[03:28] Aisha Khan: model names — redwood-13b-quant — is quantized variant safe for clinical notes? we're worried about hallucinations.
[03:36] Liam O'Rourke: good call — quantized models can slightly affect output distribution. for high-sensitivity text we recommend conservative prompting and the verified model family — we can run evals against your prompt set. Optimize has a quality monitoring feature that alerts on regression.
[03:49] Natalie Vu: do you have SOC2 docs we can share with procurement?
[03:52] Maya Chen: yes, will share SOC2 + ISO docs and the private deployment compliance pack.
[03:58] Tom Reyes: about cost — if we run a POC what are costs for hosted vs dedicated?
[04:04] Maya Chen: hosted is usage-based, per-token. Dedicated has commit pricing and lower unit cost if you need steady throughput. we can send a cost model based on your expected RPS.
[04:12] [04:30] Jorge Morales: are there constraints on prompt length or caching? we're using long context for patient history.
[04:19] Liam O'Rourke: we support long context; runtime will pick optimized kernels. caching: prefix/KV caching can drastically reduce costs for repeated contexts. but for PHI where you can't cache persistently, we recommend ephemeral caching with encryption.
[04:31] Aisha Khan: can you show the Console? want to see where billing and Optimize suggestions live.
[04:35] Maya Chen: sure i'll share my screen — okay console, top left is project selector, under Optimize you'll see suggestions for batching, quantization, and cache settings based on your token distribution.
[04:49] [silent file share noise]
[05:02] Ravi Patel: note the Optimize tips are advisory — we can apply recommended profiles automatically in Dedicated if you want.
[05:09] Natalie Vu: automatic changes worry security teams — would need an approval workflow.
[05:13] Maya Chen: we have RBAC and an approvals flag. auto-apply can be turned off, and ops changes show up in the audit log.
[05:21] Tom Reyes: audit logs retention — how long, and can we ship them to our SIEM?
[05:25] Liam O'Rourke: retention configurable per plan. yes we can stream logs to customer SIEM via secure forwarding (SQS / PubSub / Event Hubs). we'll include the schema.
[05:33] Aisha Khan: ok, question on SDK CI: best practice for rotating keys in CI pipelines?
[05:37] Ravi Patel: use short-lived tokens issued via KMS or workload identity, rotate them often. avoid baking long-lived keys into CI. we include a GitHub Actions example in the repo.
[05:48] Jorge Morales: could you give a concrete example of the KMS unwrap flow? it sounded like token_from_kms earlier but need actual steps.
[05:54] Liam O'Rourke: sure — high level: 1) store envelope key in your KMS, 2) CI or instance uses KMS to unwrap envelope key locally, 3) local helper exchanges envelope for short-lived Redwood token via a signed request, 4) token used by SDK. we'll provide the curl/sample script.
[06:10] [06:40] Maya Chen: quick pause — any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:43] Tom Reyes: primary blocker is VLAN/CIDR confirmation from our infra team and permission for peering.
[06:48] Natalie Vu: procurement needs SOC2 + processor addendum for PHI — I'd like that in writing.
[06:54] Aisha Khan: plus we want a small throughput test: 100 concurrent chat sessions with typical prompt set. can Redwood run that from sandbox?
[06:59] Liam O'Rourke: yes we can run an internal synthetic benchmark and share scripts — would like your sample prompts to be representative, redacting PHI if necessary.
[07:08] [08:00] Ravi Patel: sharing repo link in chat: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples (note: example link, will send actual). includes py/ts quickstarts, kms helper, gcp workload identity examples, and GH actions snippet.
[07:25] Jorge Morales: cool. on model variants — can we pin to older model for consistency? we prefer version pinning.
[07:29] Maya Chen: yes you can pin model version at route level. Console shows pinned version and rollouts for canary.
[07:35] Natalie Vu: do you have an SLA for Private deployments?
[07:38] Maya Chen: Dedicated/private have SLA options — we'll include the SLA doc in the packet. blackout windows will be coordinated.
[07:43] Tom Reyes: for the POC, do you have a template for benchmarks? we'd like to capture latency percentiles and token cost.
[07:49] Liam O'Rourke: we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet with p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens per request, and cost estimates.
[07:55] Aisha Khan: timeline check — if we get docs this week and set up VPC next week, is a 2-week POC feasible?
[07:59] Maya Chen: yes, 2-week POC is reasonable. we usually do a 1-week smoke + 1-week throughput.
[08:07] [08:30] Ravi Patel: small gotcha when using long contexts: make sure to tune your batching window, otherwise latency can spike. Optimize suggests a batching config for your token distribution.
[08:40] Jorge Morales: any special requirements for log redaction when shipping to SIEM? we need to ensure PHI never leaves.
[08:45] Liam O'Rourke: we support field-level redaction at the edge and deterministic hashing. recommend redaction before forwarding. we'll include examples.
[08:55] Natalie Vu: one more security question — who has access to the audit logs in Redwood?
[08:59] Maya Chen: by default, project admins. you can configure role-based access and SIEM forwarding. access is logged and auditable.
[09:06] [09:30] Aisha Khan: ok let's recap next steps.
[09:33] Maya Chen: recap: we'll send KMS runbook, SOC2 + compliance pack, terraform VPC examples, benchmark scripts and spreadsheet, and pricing. Sierra will provision sandbox VPC and confirm CIDR. schedule POC start tentative 2025-11-10.
[09:51] Tom Reyes: noted. we'll aim for 2025-11-07 to have peering ready.
[09:56] Natalie Vu: I'll compile compliance questions and get back by 2025-11-05.
[10:01] Jorge Morales: I'll redact and send a sample prompt set by 2025-11-06.
[10:07] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.
[10:12] Aisha Khan: thanks all, that was helpful.
[10:15] [Call ends]
